title: Minimax Pointwise Estimation of the Conditional Log Risk Ratio with Rough Nuisances

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the same-class n^(-2/7) upper and lower root-risk bounds using a quadratic estimator and an explicit fixed-uniform mixture, plus the n^(-1/3) known-propensity frontier and conservative interval coverage. The math and decision panels passed with no findings. The general referee capped the completed one-dimensional exact-uniform package at subfield; a realistic-design extension or calibrated inference would require a new research program.
tldr: For the causal conditional log risk ratio at \(x_0=1/2\) in the fixed one-dimensional exact-uniform class, the localized quadratic orthogonal root estimator has root mean-squared error of exact minimax order \(n^{-2/7}\). The matching converse is completed by a fixed-uniform Bernoulli mixture with exact one-observation cancellation, simultaneous class membership, a uniform every-sign likelihood-inner-product influence bound, and product-mixture chi-square control, followed by an explicit testing reduction. Supplying the propensity changes the matched frontier to \(n^{-1/3}\), and a bias-aware conservative interval has uniform coverage and length of order \(n^{-2/7}\). The exponent matches the low-smoothness elbow known for additive CATE, but the present multiplicative class and the Kennedy et al. additive-CATE class are incomparable; the contribution is the completed exact-uniform multiplicative theorem and lower construction, not a novel exponent.
gap: Published conditional relative-risk learners provide orthogonal losses and ratio inference under first-stage conditions, while published pointwise minimax theory treats an additive conditional effect and uses a lower experiment that does not preserve an exactly uniform covariate law. The exact-uniform smooth-CATE companion does not subsume the present class because \(b_P\{\exp(\theta_P)-1\}\) can be only \(1/8\)-Hölder.
fill: The project defines the at-point target through the unique continuous observed-law risk representatives, uses a positive common-weight ratio and a localized quadratic correction for the upper bound, then makes an overlapping fixed-uniform Bernoulli mixture the explicit open proof boundary for the matching converse.
